title: Bus Fault Finder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Serial Communication for Robotics
description: Read eight symptom reports from a servo bus, each with a scan result and the bytes received, and choose the most likely of six causes: wrong port, no motor power, baud rate mismatch, duplicate ID, broken chain link, or noise and a missing ground. Used in Chapter 4.

learningObjectives: Differentiate six causes of serial bus failure by choosing the most likely cause for each of eight symptom reports, with at least 6 of 8 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Compare similar-looking failures and separate them by the evidence in the scan result and the raw bytes
keyQuestions: What is the difference between silence and garbage?
Why does a partial scan point to the chain and not to the adapter?
commonMisconceptions: Silence always means the motor is broken
Garbage means the cable is bad
A partial scan means a bad adapter
assessmentOpportunities: Eight committed choices, one attempt each; 6 of 8 for mastery

controls.label: Wrong port / No motor power / Baud rate mismatch / Duplicate ID / Broken chain link / Noise or missing ground
